content: Letermovir interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, as well as other mechanisms such as P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters and OATP1B1/3 inhibition. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, necessitating careful monitoring, dosage adjustments, or the use of alternative therapies. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions and their clinical implications: 1. Repotrectinib: Letermovir increases repotrectinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. Monitor closely. 2. Ribociclib: Letermovir increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. In serious cases, consider alternative therapy. 3. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases letermovir levels by inducing P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. Monitor closely. 4. Rifaximin: Letermovir increases rifaximin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Rimegepant: Letermovir increases rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid repeating rimegepant doses within 48 hours if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 6. Risperidone: Letermovir increases risperidone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism, and letermovir increases ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Rivaroxaban: Letermovir increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Rosiglitazone: Letermovir increases rosiglitazone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution, monitor glucose concentrations, and monitor closely. 10. Rosuvastatin: Letermovir increases rosuvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. When coadministered with cyclosporine, the rosuvastatin dose should not exceed 5 mg daily. Monitor for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 11. Salmeterol: Letermovir increases salmeterol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Saxagliptin: Letermovir increases saxagliptin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Seladelpar: Letermovir increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers coadministered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 14. Selumetinib: Letermovir increases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage and monitor closely. 15. Sertraline: Letermovir increases sertraline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Sildenafil: Letermovir increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects, including respiratory depression. 17. Simvastatin: Letermovir significantly increases simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, especially when combined with cyclosporine. 18. Siponimod: Letermovir increases siponimod levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 19. Sirolimus: Letermovir increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sirolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir. Adjust sirolimus doses accordingly. When coadministered with cyclosporine, sirolimus should be taken 4 hours after cyclosporine administration. 20. Solifenacin: Letermovir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Sorafenib: Letermovir increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Sotorasib: Sotorasib decreases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 23. Sparsentan: Letermovir increases sparsentan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 24. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 25. Sufentanil: Letermovir increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of respiratory depression. 26. Sunitinib: Letermovir increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Tacrolimus: Tacrolimus increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism, and letermovir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor tacrolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir. Adjust tacrolimus doses accordingly. 28. Tadalafil: Letermovir increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Tamoxifen: Letermovir increases tamoxifen levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Tazemetostat: Letermovir increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose and monitor closely. 31. Telmisartan: Telmisartan increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases telmisartan levels via OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Tenofovir (AF and DF): Both tenofovir AF and DF decrease letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Tepotinib: Tepotinib increases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. 34. Teriflunomide: Teriflunomide increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tipranavir: Tipranavir increases letermovir levels via other mechanisms and decreases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Trofinetide: Trofinetide increases letermovir levels via OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid coadministration with sensitive substrates. 37. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Use caution and consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates. 38. Ublituximab: Ublituximab decreases letermovir effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Valsartan: Valsartan increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases valsartan levels via OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Vinblastine: Vinblastine decreases letermovir levels via P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Voclosporin: Letermovir increases voclosporin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risks. 42. Voriconazole: Letermovir decreases voriconazole levels via an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor for reduced effectiveness. 43. Voxilaprevir: Voxilaprevir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Zaleplon: Letermovir increases zaleplon levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Zanubrutinib: Letermovir increases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib dosage when coadministered and monitor closely. 46. Zileuton: Letermovir increases zileuton levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ziprasidone: Letermovir increases ziprasidone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Zolpidem: Letermovir increases zolpidem levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adverse Effects: Common side effects of letermovir include nausea (27%), diarrhea (26%), vomiting (19%), peripheral edema (14%), cough (14%), headache (14%), fatigue (13%), abdominal pain (12%), tachycardia (4%), and atrial fibrillation (3%). Pregnancy and Lactation: No data are available on the use of letermovir in pregnant women. Letermovir is present in the milk of lactating rats, but its presence in human breast milk is unknown. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug. Administration: Letermovir injection should only be used in patients unable to take oral therapy and should not exceed 4 weeks of intravenous administration. The solution must be diluted before IV use and inspected for discoloration or particulates.
